# Kalle Westerling

> Kalle Westerling is a Staff Developer Relations Engineer at Chainguard, where he builds courses, labs and workshops on software supply chain security.

Website: https://westerling.nu/
Role: Staff Developer Relations Engineer at Chainguard (https://www.chainguard.dev)
Contact: kallewesterling@gmail.com. For talks, workshops, podcasts and anything about developer education or software supply chain security.

## About

I teach developers how to ship secure software, and I build the tools that make that teaching hold up. At Chainguard I create courses, hands-on labs, workshops and live demos on container images, open-source libraries and software supply chain security.

I came to developer relations by way of the classroom and the research lab: a PhD in digital humanities, coding curricula for faculty across the United States, and research software at the Alan Turing Institute. I still design learning the same way: start from where people get stuck, and remove that step.

Kalle Westerling is a Staff Developer Relations Engineer at Chainguard, where he creates courses, hands-on labs, workshops and live demos that help developers adopt secure container images and open-source libraries. He also builds open-source tools for developer educators, from testing code examples in published courses to pacing live sessions. Before Chainguard he was a research software engineer and research application manager at the Alan Turing Institute, and before that he led national coding and research training programs at CUNY, where he earned a PhD in digital humanities. He still approaches technical education as a teacher first.

## Tools I build

### cvediff

Security. Compares the known CVEs in two container images side by side in the terminal. Answers one question fast: what changes if we swap this base image for a hardened one?
Stack: Python, Grype, CLI.
Code: https://github.com/kallewesterling/cvediff

### errata

Docs quality. Finds broken code examples inside published course content, and keeps a dated record of the ones you can't fix yet. Courses stay live; the code in them shouldn't rot.
Stack: TypeScript, CI.
Code: https://github.com/kallewesterling/errata

### CodexMachina

Docs as code. Extracts, runs and lints the code blocks in Markdown and HTML documentation, with output verification, so every example in the docs is one you can trust.
Stack: Go, Markdown.

### session-pacer

Speaking. A presenter view for timed talks, workshops and demos. Shows the notes for the current section, tells you when you're behind, and suggests what to cut.
Stack: HTML, JavaScript.
App: https://westerling.nu/session-pacer/
Code: https://github.com/kallewesterling/session-pacer

### syncjar

Course ops. Edit, preview and sync Skilljar course content locally, so course authors get a real git workflow instead of a web form.
Stack: Node.js, Skilljar API.
Docs: https://westerling.nu/syncjar/
Code: https://github.com/kallewesterling/syncjar

### credjar

Course ops. Inspect, issue and revoke Credly badges from the command line, for certification programs that outgrow spreadsheets.
Stack: Node.js, Credly API.
Docs: https://westerling.nu/credjar/
Code: https://github.com/kallewesterling/credjar

## Research software

Before Chainguard I spent four years building and maintaining research software at the Alan Turing Institute: open-source Python tools, their documentation, and the communities around them.

- [MapReader](https://mapreader.readthedocs.io/en/latest/), Documentation and community: A computer vision pipeline for exploring and analysing large collections of digitised maps. Winner of the 2023 Roy Rosenzweig Prize for Innovation in Digital History.
- [AutoEmulate](https://github.com/alan-turing-institute/autoemulate), Contributor: A Python package for semi-automated emulation of complex simulations, built for digital twin research.
- [TEA Platform](https://assuranceplatform.turing.ac.uk/), Contributor: The Trustworthy and Ethical Assurance platform, a collaborative tool for building structured arguments that an AI system was developed responsibly.

Papers:

- [AutoEmulate: a PyTorch tool for end-to-end emulation workflows](https://doi.org/10.21105/joss.10087). Journal of Open Source Software, 2026.
- [MapReader: software and principles for computational map studies](https://read.uolpress.co.uk/read/7526964a-e6de-41e8-8769-2b0df46b4a25/section/e85a784b-c363-4478-b92e-bee17c5dc6ff). Living with Machines, University of London Press, 2025.
- [AutoEmulate: a Python package for semi-automated emulation](https://doi.org/10.21105/joss.07626). Journal of Open Source Software, 2025.
- [MapReader: open software for the visual analysis of maps](https://doi.org/10.21105/joss.06434). Journal of Open Source Software, 2024.
- [Fair by design: a sociotechnical approach to justifying the fairness of AI-enabled systems across the lifecycle](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.09029). arXiv, 2024.

## Capture the flag and games

Some security lessons only stick when you do them yourself, against the clock, with a team. So alongside talks and courses I design games: capture the flag events and card games that put developers in the attacker's seat and then hand them the fix.

- Hands on, not slides: Every challenge ends in something you did yourself, at a terminal or around a table. You don't leave having watched someone else do it.
- Built for mixed rooms: Beginner, standard and advanced editions, so a room of first-time coders and a room of platform engineers both get a real challenge.
- Runs anywhere: Customer offices, partner events, community meetups and conference floors, from a small room to a couple of hundred players.

### Operation Lockdown

Capture the flag. A team capture-the-flag in two halves. First you break in: exploit the weaknesses in a container image and its software supply chain. Then you fix them the secure way. Run for customers, partners and communities. Editions: Standard, Advanced, Beginner. Played in Paris · Dresden · Stockholm.

### Faithful by Default

Capture the flag. A themed edition of Operation Lockdown, run together with Somerford. Same attack-then-fix format, new theme. Played in London.

### Cards Against Vulnerabilities

Card game. A security card game I designed for conference floors. First played at the RSA Conference AppSec Village, then scaled to about 200 players at DEF CON 34. Played in San Francisco · Las Vegas.

Want a CTF at your event, meetup or team offsite? I can adapt the format and the difficulty to your room.

## Experience

### Developer relations (2025–now)

**Staff Developer Relations Engineer**, Chainguard (Feb 2025–now)

- Courses, learning paths and certifications on Chainguard Courses, from first draft to badge.
- Operation Lockdown, a capture-the-flag format run for customers and partners in Paris, Dresden and London.
- Designed Cards Against Vulnerabilities, a security card game first played at the RSA Conference AppSec Village and scaled to about 200 players at DEF CON 34.
- Talks, demos and monthly Learning Labs on container images, libraries and secure agent workflows, plus a full 2026 conference circuit across Europe and the U.S.
- Partner certification paths and hands-on enablement workshops for customers.
- Convened a cross-company training council to align customer, partner and internal training.
- Open-source tooling that tests course code and scripts course operations.

### Research software (2021–2025)

**Research Application Manager**, Alan Turing Institute, Data/Culture and Digital Twins research (2023–2025)

- Built sustainable communities around open-source research tools, including MapReader, AutoEmulate and the TEA Platform.
- Co-authored three papers in the Journal of Open Source Software.
- Kept the user perspective at the centre of research software development.

**Research Software Engineer**, Living with Machines, British Library and Alan Turing Institute (2021–2023)

- Built four Python packages and documented three of them end to end.
- Made 40+ data visualisations in JavaScript and D3.
- Visualisations shown at Leeds City Museum, seen by more than 40,000 visitors.

### Teaching and community (2011–2021)

**Project Manager, Digital Humanities Research Institutes**, The Graduate Center, CUNY (2018–2021)

- Ran the NEH-funded "Expanding Communities of Practice" program for faculty and librarians across the U.S.
- Co-wrote the open DHRI coding curriculum, with over 2,000 commits.

**Scholars Program Manager and Steering Committee member**, HASTAC

- Managed a fellowship network of graduate students across many universities.

**Instructor**, CUNY, NYU and Villanova University

- Taught theatre history, performance and digital media courses.

## At work

I'm a Staff Developer Relations Engineer at [Chainguard](https://www.chainguard.dev), wrapping up a busy 2026 on the conference circuit in Europe and the U.S.

- **Capture the flag season.** In the past few weeks I've run Operation Lockdown in Paris and an advanced edition in Dresden, and Faithful by Default with Somerford in London. [More about the games](/#games).

## On the side

I'm building small tools for the friction I hit in my own teaching:

- [session-pacer](/session-pacer/), for keeping live sessions on time.
- [errata](https://github.com/kallewesterling/errata) and CodexMachina, for catching broken code examples in published courses and docs.
- [cvediff](https://github.com/kallewesterling/cvediff), for comparing the CVEs in two container images.

And one that goes back to my research roots: a data project on Swedish theatre history.
